Skew t distribution of Jones and Faddy

Source: R/skew_t.R
skew_t.Rd

Density, distribution function, quantile function and random generation for the skew t distribution of Jones and Faddy (2003), standardized to mean zero and unit variance.

Usage

dskew_t(x, df_left, df_right, log = FALSE)

pskew_t(q, df_left, df_right)

qskew_t(p, df_left, df_right)

rskew_t(n, df_left, df_right)

Arguments

x, q

Vector of quantiles.

df_left, df_right

Degrees of freedom of the left and the right tail, greater than 2.

log

Logical; if TRUE, the log density is returned.

p

Vector of probabilities.

n

Number of draws.

Value

Numeric vector.

Details

Before standardization, the density with parameters \(a, b > 0\) is $$f(t) = C \left(1 + \frac{t}{\sqrt{a + b + t^2}}\right)^{a + 1/2} \left(1 - \frac{t}{\sqrt{a + b + t^2}}\right)^{b + 1/2}, \qquad C = \frac{1}{2^{a + b - 1} B(a, b) \sqrt{a + b}}.$$ The left tail decays like a Student t with \(2a\) degrees of freedom and the right tail like a Student t with \(2b\) degrees of freedom. The functions use df_left = 2a and df_right = 2b. If they are equal, the distribution is the Student t distribution scaled to unit variance. If df_left < df_right, the left tail is heavier and the distribution is skewed to the left. Both must be greater than 2 for the variance to exist.

The density is smooth everywhere. This is important for the Laplace approximation, which uses the second derivative of the log density.

References

Jones, M. C. and Faddy, M. J. (2003). A skew extension of the t-distribution, with applications. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 65(1), 159-174. doi:10.1111/1467-9868.00378
